verdict.rationale: WezTerm's built-in multiplexer (unix/SSH domains, a daemonizable mux server) keeps tabs and panes alive so a GUI client can reconnect after closing or disconnecting. That covers surviving a GUI restart or disconnect, but not true save-and-restore of layout after a full machine restart or a crash of the multiplexer itself. missing for 10: documented session save/restore of windows, tabs and layout across a full restart or crash, restoration of each pane's working directory, and hands-on corroboration of recovery after a crash.

support.subject: As a developer, I can restore my windows, tabs, and working directories after a restart or crash

citations.quote: an alternative configuration that connects to a remote wezterm instance and preserves your tabs.
you can enable local terminal multiplexing with features similar to those in tmux or screen.
Uses it as mosh+tmux-like reconnectable sessions with panes and tabs from a Mac laptop to a Linux work machine
`wezterm-mux-server --daemonize`, then `wezterm cli spawn --new-window` returned a pane-id
